podcast.body: This was George W. Johnson's most popular track, recorded in 1890 using Thomas Edison's wax cylinders. By 1894, it became the best-selling song ever, reaching number one on the nascent music charts and making Johnson the first Black performer to top those charts. "Johnson's most popular track was The Laughing Song, which was recorded in 1890."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: A later recording of "The Laughing Song" was made in 1897. Due to the inability to reproduce wax cylinders, Johnson had to record each cylinder individually, sometimes singing the song 50 times a day, leading to estimates of 12,000-15,000 performances to meet orders for 50,000 copies. "All I can tell you is that it was a later recording from 1897."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
